sources.name: Census 2021, TS054 Tenure (households, by LSOA)
sources.publisher: Office for National Statistics, via Nomis
sources.caveat: A count of households on census day. Council stock changes (right to buy, sales, new build), so today's figure can differ.

sources.name: English Indices of Deprivation 2025: income score, deciles and population (File 7)
sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.vintage: Published 2025; population is the mid-2022 estimate
sources.caveat: Ranks areas against each other (England-wide); it does not measure how much more deprived one is than another.

sources.name: Income estimates for small areas, England and Wales, FYE 2023 (MSOA)
sources.caveat: Model-based estimate (survey data modelled to small areas), not a count. Published for areas of ~8,000 people, so every neighbourhood inherits its MSOA's figure; a confidence interval is published and shown.

sources.name: Street-level crime
sources.publisher: data.police.uk (police forces of England and Wales)
sources.caveat: Crimes recorded by police, not all crimes committed. Locations are snapped to the nearest anonymised street point. Counted here by the neighbourhood that point falls in. Busy centres record visitors' crimes; it says little about how safe a street feels.

sources.name: Food Hygiene Rating Scheme establishments
sources.caveat: Used only as a footfall proxy to flag busy centres (food premises per resident); not a count of people.

sources.name: LSOA (December 2021) boundaries, generalised (BGC V5)
sources.caveat: Generalised (simplified) outlines, accurate to a few tens of metres; crimes right on an edge can land in the neighbouring area.
